scope: Shared filmmaking knowledge; never project canon or permission to execute

principles.title: Sensor size and focal length determine angular coverage
principles.statement: For an ideal rectilinear camera, a larger active sensor dimension widens the corresponding angle of view at fixed focal length. A longer focal length narrows it.
assumptions: Rectilinear projection
Matching sensor axis and active crop
Ignores lens distortion, close-focus extension and focus breathing
Anamorphic and VR cameras require their own models
principles.example: A 36 mm active width with a 50 mm lens gives about 39.6 degrees horizontal coverage under these assumptions.
principles.appUse: Explain framing in camera rehearsal; do not infer sensor size from the words wide shot.

sources.title: Edmund Optics: Understanding Focal Length and Field of View

principles.title: Frame rate and shutter angle determine exposure duration
principles.statement: Exposure duration changes when capture rate changes at fixed shutter angle. The intended blur still depends on movement and camera behavior.
assumptions: Camera-specific supported settings must also be checked
Capture rate is distinct from playback rate
This equation alone does not predict flicker, rolling shutter or final motion quality
principles.example: At 24 fps and 180 degrees, each exposure is 1/48 second. 180 degrees is a choice, not a mandatory creative rule.
principles.appUse: Show exposure duration beside camera timing; keep unsupported provider settings as intentions only.

principles.title: Focus target and aperture are separate controls
principles.statement: A camera can focus at an explicit distance or on an object. Aperture affects the rendered blur around that focus. Naming a prime or zoom lens does not by itself specify depth of field.
assumptions: Simulator output depends on its camera and render model
A quantitative depth-of-field calculation also needs a chosen circle of confusion and viewing assumptions
principles.appUse: Represent focus start/end targets separately from movement and shot size; keep a focus pull distinct from a dolly.

sources.title: Blender 4.4 Manual: Cameras
sources.locator: Depth of Field and Aperture sections; retrieved indexed documentation

principles.title: Distance affects direct sound level
principles.statement: In a free field with point-source spreading, doubling source distance reduces sound pressure level by about 6 dB.
assumptions: Free field and point-source approximation
Reflections, directional radiation, occlusion and microphone proximity effects are excluded
This predicts relative level, not intelligibility or recording quality
principles.appUse: Help flag distant dialogue recording and motivate boom/lavalier planning; require actual sound review.

principles.title: Media time requires a value and a rate
principles.statement: Store the rate alongside media positions and durations, and declare whether a range end is inclusive or exclusive. Frame counts without rates are ambiguous.
assumptions: Variable-frame-rate media needs measured timestamps
Timecode labels and sample positions are different representations
OpenTimelineIO RationalTime stores a value and rate as doubles; exact rational arithmetic is not implied
principles.example: The half-open range [10, 15) contains frames 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14: five frames of duration. At 24 fps, 48 frames represent two seconds.
principles.appUse: Preserve clip rate, source trims and audio overlaps through the movie timeline and editor handoff.

principles.title: Input, working and display color transforms have different jobs
principles.statement: ACES describes an explicit path from source encoding through working representations and creative looks to output transforms. Record the chosen configuration instead of treating a look name as complete color metadata.
assumptions: ACES is an available workflow, not a forced choice for every film
Unknown source color encoding stays unknown
Named transforms do not prove a file was processed or a display calibrated
principles.appUse: Retain color metadata with media through Blender, generation returns and editorial delivery.

principles.title: Attention helps explain perceived continuity across cuts
principles.statement: Smith's Attentional Theory of Cinematic Continuity relates continuity techniques to attention and perceptual expectations. It offers a way to reason about what the viewer follows across an edit.
assumptions: A theoretical account is not a universal response predictor
Spatial disorientation may be intentional
A continuity suggestion can be overridden by the filmmaker
principles.appUse: Ask what carries across a cut and explain a possible continuity mismatch; do not grade artistic quality from a rule violation.

sources.title: Tim J. Smith: The Attentional Theory of Cinematic Continuity
sources.locator: 2012 publication record; repository manuscript dated 2011, abstract and continuity discussion

principles.title: Shared gaze does not establish shared understanding
principles.statement: In the reported experiments, prior narrative context improved comprehension while producing only subtle eye-movement differences against strong attentional synchrony.
assumptions: Results concern the studied film material and conditions
Do not infer a viewer's emotion, understanding or enjoyment solely from gaze or a model score
principles.appUse: Evaluate whether viewers understand the intended beat with a direct review question, separately from visual attention or aesthetic preference.

sources.title: Loschky et al. (2015): What Would Jaws Do?
